Devengo Closes €5 Million Funding Round
summary:
Devengo, a Spanish fintech specialising in instant account-to-account (A2A) payment infrastructure and a payment institution authorised by the Bank of Spain, has closed a new €5 million funding round combining debt and equity.
The transaction brings Mutua Madrileña (through its Mutua Ventures investment vehicle) into the company's shareholding structure, with the participation of Banco Sabadell, Bankinter, Telefónica and TheVentureCity, which are renewing their commitment to the project. The aim is to drive Devengo's growth and international expansion in a market where instant payments are moving towards global adoption and new use cases.
Banking, insurance and telecommunications back Devengo's business model
The round brings together investors from three sectors with high payment volumes – banking, insurance and telecommunications – alongside specialised venture capital. This combination reflects the industry's interest in infrastructure that enables money to be transferred between accounts instantly, securely and automatically.
“To make an international payment instant, there is no need to invent a new financial system, but rather to better connect the one that already exists. At Devengo, we are already able to offer this immediacy to regulated banks and financial institutions, and with this round we aim to reach new markets, starting with Latin America. The next step is to enable AI agents to make payments using real money and with the same guarantees as any bank transfer,” explains Fernando Cabello-Astolfi, CEO and co-founder of Devengo.
“Devengo combines strong technological capabilities with a distinctive regulatory positioning. We believe it has the attributes needed to lead the evolution of instant payments in Europe and, from the Mutua Group's perspective, we see significant potential in its solutions to transform payment processes and account ownership verification,” says Andrés Sánchez Hontoria, Head of Corporate Venture Capital at Mutua Madrileña.
First non-bank institution with a direct connection to Iberpay
Devengo provides an API-first infrastructure for executing instant, automated and programmable account-to-account (A2A) payments. Thanks to its direct connection to Iberpay, which makes it the first non-bank institution to have access to this infrastructure, Devengo enables companies and financial institutions to execute instant transfers without having to develop their own payment infrastructure. Devengo's technology automates payment processes that previously required human intervention, reducing manual tasks and operating costs. It also speeds up the receipt of funds and improves the user experience (UX), allowing recipients to access their money immediately.
Devengo currently serves companies across a range of sectors, including insurance, lending, online gaming, real estate, e-commerce and services. It also works with some of Spain's leading banking institutions and insurers, including companies that are among its shareholders.
Its infrastructure is complemented by account ownership verification services, which help companies meet their regulatory obligations and prevent fraud and payment errors.
Borderless payments without stablecoins: instant transfers for banks and AI agents
Devengo will use the funds to drive growth, accelerate international expansion and develop new products. Its priorities include two business lines: instant international transfers for banks and regulated financial institutions, with Latin America among its first target markets, and agentic payments, which will enable artificial intelligence agents to carry out transactions using real money through account-to-account transfers within a regulated and controlled framework.
While part of the sector is exploring stablecoins to speed up international payments, Devengo is betting on next-generation banking infrastructure. Its recent certification under the OCT Inst protocol, the European Payments Council (EPC) scheme that enables instant transfers in both directions between the SEPA area and the rest of the world, allows the fintech to offer this capability to banks and regulated financial institutions, which will then be able to make it available to their customers.

content: Spanish fintech Devengo has closed a €5 million funding round combining debt and equity. title: The Real Edge in Trading: EDGE Since Launch
summary:
Tradeview Markets launched the EDGE Instant Liquidity Connector in October 2026 with a simple challenge to traders: try it once and judge the fills for yourself. In the weeks since, the company has expanded EDGE with a new account tier, opened live trials to its partner network, and put raw pricing on public display.
"We told traders to try it once and look at their fills," said Tim Furey, Founder and CEO of Tradeview Markets. "That's exactly what they're doing. Once you've traded on raw pricing, it's hard to go back to a padded spread."
Tradeview Markets has opened more than 400 EDGE accounts since the October launch. 
What's new since launch
●       EDGE Premium. A second EDGE tier for traders who want more flexibility, with trades from 0.01 lots and leverage up to 1:400.
●       Four account models. Traders can now choose between EDGE, EDGE Premium, Classic ILC and XLev, depending on whether they optimize for cost, size or leverage.
●       EDGE IB Program. Active Tradeview introducing brokers can get a funded EDGE account for 30 days to experience the execution before they share it with their clients.
●       EDGE Creator Program. Approved trading content creators can get the same funded 30-day EDGE account and share their real experience with their audiences.
●       Live pricing in public. Tradeview's EDGE page streams live best bid and offer pricing on .edge symbols, so traders can see the spreads before they open an account.
Why it's resonating
Traders have long suspected that the price on their screen isn't the price the market is offering. EDGE removes that doubt. Clients see raw pricing from Tradeview's liquidity providers and pay one flat, published commission.
Behind it is a real-time AI decision engine running on Tradeview's own matching engine. EDGE scans multiple top-tier liquidity providers in milliseconds, splits larger orders where needed, and routes them to the best available price. Tradeview's trading servers sit in the LD4 data center, connected by fiber directly to its liquidity partners.
"Same pairs, different infrastructure," Furey said. "If it doesn't say .edge, it isn't EDGE."
EDGE at a glance
●       EDGE: raw spreads from 0.0 pips, USD 2 per lot per side (USD 4 round turn) on FX and USD 6 round turn on metals, from 0.10 lots, leverage up to 1:100, minimum deposit USD 2,500
●       EDGE Premium: raw spreads from 0.0 pips, USD 3 per lot per side, from 0.01 lots, leverage up to 1:400, minimum deposit USD 2,500
●       Both run on MT4 and MT5, with nothing new to install
Traders can open a demo or live EDGE account at https://info.tradeviewmarkets.com/edge-free-demo

Driven by an AI decision engine and raw pricing, EDGE provides traders with direct access to top-tier liquidity providers with tight spreads and transparent commissions.
